sw0: Jirani yangu aliinama karibu na sikio langu. Akanong'ona:
Nitakuambia ukweli. Kwa sekunde moja... nilitaka kusema ndiyo.
Naitwa Neema. Nauza samaki pale Kariakoo. Naamka saa kumi alfajiri, kila siku, kwa ajili ya watoto wangu wawili.
Binti yangu Rehema, miaka kumi na minne. Anataka kuwa daktari.
Sisi wanawake kumi na wawili tulikuwa na chama. Kila wiki, shilingi elfu ishirini. Na mwezi Desemba... ilikuwa zamu yangu. Ada yote ya Rehema ilikuwa pale.
Mweka hazina alikuwa Shangazi Rose. Tuliimba kwaya pamoja. Alimbeba mwanangu siku ya ubatizo wake.
sw1: Siku ya zamu yangu... simu yake imezimwa. Duka limefungwa. Rose ameondoka. Na shilingi milioni tatu za familia kumi na mbili.
Mnaijua aibu ile? Soko zima linakutazama. Na wewe ndiye uliyemwamini.
Ndipo jirani yule akaja na lile neno la mganga.
Lakini usiku ule, nilifungua Biblia. Na neno moja likanishika:
Wapenzi, msijilipizie kisasi. Kisasi ni juu yangu mimi; mimi nitalipa, anena Bwana. Warumi kumi na mbili, kumi na tisa.
Rehema alinisikia nikilia. Akakaa karibu nami, akasema: Mama, naweza kusubiri mwaka mmoja.
sw2: Moyo wangu ulivunjika. Nikamwambia: hapana, mwanangu. Huu si mzigo wako.
Jumapili, Mchungaji aliwakusanya wanawake wa chama. Hatukuomba dhidi ya Rose. Tuliomba kwa ajili ya watoto wetu.
Mkuu wa shule akaniruhusu kulipa ada kwa awamu tatu. Nikaongeza biashara ya jioni. Rehema akasomea mezani, kati ya wateja.
Miezi saba baadaye... mlango ukagongwa. Alikuwa Rose.
Amekonda. Mikono inatetemeka. Akanipa bahasha. Haikuwa yote... lakini ilikuwa mwanzo.
Sijasahau. Lakini nimesamehe. Na leo, Rehema ni wa kwanza darasani kwa sayansi.
sw3: Na wewe je? Umewahi kusalitiwa na mtu uliyemwamini? Niandikie kwenye maoni. Na mtumie dada yako video hii kwenye WhatsApp.

en0: My neighbor leaned in close to my ear. And she whispered:
I'll tell you the truth. For one second... I wanted to say yes.
My name is Neema. I sell fish at Kariakoo market. I get up at four in the morning, every day, for my two children.
My daughter Rehema is fourteen. She wants to be a doctor.
Twelve of us women had a savings circle, a chama. Every week, twenty thousand shillings. And in December... it was my turn. Every cent of Rehema's school fees was in that pot.
The treasurer was Auntie Rose. We sang in the choir together. She held my son on the day he was baptized.
en1: On my day... her phone was off. Her shop was locked. Rose was gone. With three million shillings from twelve families.
Do you know that kind of shame? The whole market watching you. And you were the one who trusted her.
That's when my neighbor came with her word about the witch doctor.
But that night, I opened my Bible. And one verse took hold of me:
Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves. Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord. Romans twelve, nineteen.
Rehema heard me crying. She sat down beside me and said: Mama, I can wait a year.
en2: It broke my heart. I told her: no, my child. This is not your load to carry.
That Sunday, the pastor gathered the women of the chama. We did not pray against Rose. We prayed for our children.
The headmaster let me pay the fees in three parts. I added an evening stall. Rehema did her homework at my table, between customers.
Seven months later... a knock at the door. It was Rose.
She was thin. Her hands were shaking. She handed me an envelope. It wasn't all of it... but it was a start.
I haven't forgotten. But I have forgiven. And today, Rehema is first in her class in science.
en3: And you? Have you ever been betrayed by someone you trusted? Tell me in the comments. And send this to a sister on WhatsApp.

fr0: Je vais vous raconter une histoire. Une histoire de trahison, de larmes... et de grâce. Restez avec moi jusqu'à la fin, parce que la fin, personne ne l'attendait.
es0: Déjame contarte una historia. Una historia de traición, de lágrimas... y de gracia. Quédate conmigo hasta el final, porque ese final nadie lo esperaba.
